nodes.name: The first step and correctness
nodes.statement: Finally, on symbols $(\sigma_{-1},\sigma_{0},\sigma_{+1},S)$ we are in state $q_0$ and simulate the first two steps of the Turing machine $M$. Also, we replace $S$ according to the movement of the head. This guarantees that $M'$ will only read such a symbol in the very first step and hence computes two steps of $M$ in one step exactly once. It is not difficult to see that $M'$ accepts $x'$ in $k-1$ steps if and only if $M$ accepts $x$ in $k$ steps.
nodes.statement_short: The $S$-marker is read exactly once, so exactly two $M$-steps are merged.

nodes.name: Proof of the semi-strict framework theorem
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a parameterized problem whose unparameterized version is \NP{}-hard and it holds that $\{(x,k)\in L\mid k\le c\}\in \PTIME{}$, for a constant $c\geq 1$. Let $\calD$ be a strong parameter diminisher for $L$ with constant $c_d\geq 2$ and let $\calA$ be a semi-strict polynomial kernelization for~$L$ with constant~$c_a>1$. \iflong{}We show that we can solve any instance $(x,k)$ of $L$, with $k$ being the parameter, in polynomial time. \fi{} Let $(x,k)$ be an instance of $L$. Apply $\calD$ on $(x,k)$ exactly $c_r:=\lceil\log_{c_d}(c_a+c_d)\rceil$~times to obtain an equivalent instance $\calD^{c_r}(x,k)=(x',k')$ with $k'\leq k/c_d^{c_r}\leq k/(c_a+c_d)$. Observe that the size of~$|(x', k')|$ is still polynomial in $|(x, k)|$ as $c_r$ is a constant. Next, apply $\calA$ on $(x',k')$ to obtain an equivalent instance $(x'',k'')$ with $|(x'', k'')|\leq k'^{c'}$, $c'\geq 1$, and $k''\leq c_a\cdot k'\leq c_a\cdot k/(c_a+c_d)<k$. Repeating the described procedure at most $k$ times produces an instance $(y,1)$ of $L$, solvable in polynomial time.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the strong diminisher $\lceil\log_{c_d}(c_a+c_d)\rceil$ times so the semi-strict kernel's factor $c_a$ cannot restore the parameter.

nodes.name: Hypotheses
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a parameterized problem whose unparameterized version is \NP{}-hard and it holds that $\{(x,k)\in L\mid k\le c\}\in \PTIME{}$, for a constant $c\geq 1$.

nodes.name: Fix strong diminisher and semi-strict kernelization
nodes.statement: Let $\calD$ be a strong parameter diminisher for $L$ with constant $c_d\geq 2$ and let $\calA$ be a semi-strict polynomial kernelization for~$L$ with constant~$c_a>1$. \iflong{}We show that we can solve any instance $(x,k)$ of $L$, with $k$ being the parameter, in polynomial time. \fi{} Let $(x,k)$ be an instance of $L$.
nodes.statement_short: Name $\calD$ with factor $c_d\geq2$, $\calA$ with factor $c_a>1$, and an arbitrary instance.

nodes.name: Apply the strong diminisher $c_r$ times
nodes.statement: Apply $\calD$ on $(x,k)$ exactly $c_r:=\lceil\log_{c_d}(c_a+c_d)\rceil$~times to obtain an equivalent instance $\calD^{c_r}(x,k)=(x',k')$ with $k'\leq k/c_d^{c_r}\leq k/(c_a+c_d)$. Observe that the size of~$|(x', k')|$ is still polynomial in $|(x, k)|$ as $c_r$ is a constant.
nodes.statement_short: Drive the parameter down to $k/(c_a+c_d)$ at polynomial size cost.

nodes.name: Apply the semi-strict kernelization
nodes.statement: Next, apply $\calA$ on $(x',k')$ to obtain an equivalent instance $(x'',k'')$ with $|(x'', k'')|\leq k'^{c'}$, $c'\geq 1$, and $k''\leq c_a\cdot k'\leq c_a\cdot k/(c_a+c_d)<k$.
nodes.statement_short: The multiplicative blow-up $c_a$ still leaves $k''<k$.

nodes.name: Iterate to parameter one
nodes.statement: Repeating the described procedure at most $k$ times produces an instance $(y,1)$ of $L$, solvable in polynomial time.
nodes.statement_short: At most $k$ rounds give a polynomial-time solvable instance, so P=NP.

If $k$ is odd, then we add a unique element to~$U$, a unique set containing only this element to~$\mathcal{F}$, and we set~$k=k+1$. Hence, we assume that~$k$~is even. The following procedure is a strong parameter diminisher for the problem parameterized by $k\log n$. Let $U' = U$ and for all~$F_i, F_j$ create $F'_{\{i, j\}} = F_i \cup F_j$. Let $\mathcal{F}' = \{F'_{\{i, j\}} \ | \ i\neq j\}$ and set $k' = k/2$. This yields the instance~$(U', \mathcal{F}', k')$ of \pprob{Set Cover}{k\log n} in polynomial time. \iflong{}In the following we \else{}It remains to \fi{}show that $(U, \mathcal{F}, k)$ is a yes-instance if and only if $(U', \mathcal{F}', k')$ is a yes-instance\iflong{}. Furthermore, we argue that \else{}, as well that \fi{}$k'\log n' < (k\log n)/c$ for some constant~$c>1$, where $n'=|U'|$. \toappendix { Assume that there is a set cover $\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ for~$U$ of size~$k$. Let $\mathcal{C} = \{C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k\}$ and let $\mathcal{C}' = \{C_1\cup C_2, C_3\cup C_4, \ldots, C_{k-1}\cup C_k\}$. Then clearly $\mathcal{C}'\subseteq \mathcal{F}'$ is a set cover for~$U'$ of size~$k/2$. Conversely, assume that there is a set cover $\mathcal{C}'$ for $U'$ of size $k/2$. Let $\mathcal{C}' = \{C_1', C_2', \ldots, C_{k/2}'\}$, let $C_i'=C_i\cup C_{i'}$ and let $\mathcal{C} = \{C_1, C_{1'}, C_2, C_{2'},\ldots,C_{k/2},C_{k/2'}\}$. Then clearly $\mathcal{C}\subseteq \mathcal{F}$ is a set cover for $U$ of size at most~$k$. Furthermore, we have that $m' = {m \choose 2}$. It follows that \[k'\log n' \leq \frac{k+1}{2}\log (n+1) \stackrel{k\geq 2}{\leq} \frac{3k}{4}\log (n+1) \leq \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}k\log ((n+1)^{\sqrt{3}/2}) \stackrel{n\geq 5}{\leq} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}k\log (n).\] Note that in the first inequality, we consider the cases of $k$ being modified to be even. It follows that for $k>2$ the parameter decreases by at least a factor of $\sqrt{3}/{2}$ and for $k=2$ the parameter diminisher produces either a trivial yes- or a trivial no-instance. } It is easy to see that a strong parameter diminisher for \pprob{Hitting Set}{k \log m} can be constructed in a similar fashion.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\mathcal{F}$ by all pairwise unions and halve $k$; this is a strong diminisher for the parameter $k\log n$.

nodes.name: Fix instance and normalizing bounds
nodes.statement: Let $(U, \mathcal{F} = \{F_1, \ldots, F_m\}, k)$ be an instance of \pprob{Set Cover}{k\log n} and assume that~$k\geq 2$ and $n\geq 5$.

nodes.name: The pairwise-union diminisher
nodes.statement: The following procedure is a strong parameter diminisher for the problem parameterized by $k\log n$. Let $U' = U$ and for all~$F_i, F_j$ create $F'_{\{i, j\}} = F_i \cup F_j$. Furthermore, we argue that \else{}, as well that \fi{}$k'\log n' < (k\log n)/c$ for some constant~$c>1$, where $n'=|U'|$.

nodes.name: Forward direction
nodes.statement: Assume that there is a set cover $\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ for~$U$ of size~$k$. Then clearly $\mathcal{C}'\subseteq \mathcal{F}'$ is a set cover for~$U'$ of size~$k/2$.

nodes.name: Converse direction
nodes.statement: Conversely, assume that there is a set cover $\mathcal{C}'$ for $U'$ of size $k/2$. nodes.name: Parameter drops by a constant factor
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we have that $m' = {m \choose 2}$. It follows that \[k'\log n' \leq \frac{k+1}{2}\log (n+1) \stackrel{k\geq 2}{\leq} \frac{3k}{4}\log (n+1) \leq \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}k\log ((n+1)^{\sqrt{3}/2}) \stackrel{n\geq 5}{\leq} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}k\log (n).\] Note that in the first inequality, we consider the cases of $k$ being modified to be even. It follows that for $k>2$ the parameter decreases by at least a factor of $\sqrt{3}/{2}$ and for $k=2$ the parameter diminisher produces either a trivial yes- or a trivial no-instance.

nodes.statement: It is easy to see that a strong parameter diminisher for \pprob{Hitting Set}{k \log m} can be constructed in a similar fashion.

nodes.name: Proof that strong diminishers speed up algorithms
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a parameterized problem. Let $\calA$ be an algorithm that solves any instance~$(x,k)\in L$ in~$2^{c_1\cdot k}\cdot |x|^{c_2}$~time with constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and let~$\calD$ be a strong parameter diminisher for $L$ with constant~$d\geq 2$. Recall that by definition of a strong parameter diminisher, the size of the instance grows at most polynomially each time $\calD$ is applied. Let $b\geq 1$ be a constant such that the size of the instance obtained by applying $\calD$ once to $(x,k)$ is upper-bounded by $|x|^b$. We set~$\cmin:=\min\{2,b\}$. Let~$f:L\to\N$ be a function such that $f(x, k)\ge c$ for all $(x, k)\in L$ with $|x|\ge c_0$ for some constant~$c_0\in\N$. Let $(x',k')$ be the instance of $L$ obtained by applying $\calD$ $\lceil\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)\rceil$ times to instance~$(x,k)\in L$ with $|x|\geq c_0$. We obtain \[ |x'| \leq |x|^{b^{\lceil\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)\rceil}} \leq |x|^{b^{2\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)}} \leq |x|^{f(x,k)^{c_3}},\, \text{for some constant $c_3\geq 1$.} \] Furthermore, the parameter decreases by the constant factor~$d$ each time the diminisher is applied, hence \[ k' = k/d^{\lceil\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)\rceil}\leq k/d^{\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)} \leq k/d^{\log_{d} f(x,k)}\leq k/f(x,k) . \] Finally, applying $\calA$ on $(x', k')$ solves $(x',k')$ in time \[2^{c_1\cdot k'}\cdot |x'|^{c_2} \leq 2^{c_1\cdot k/f(x,k)}\cdot |x|^{c_2\cdot f(x,k)^{c_3}} \in 2^{O(k/ f(x,k))}\cdot |x|^{f(x,k)^{O(1)}}.\qedhere\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the diminisher $\lceil\log_c f(x,k)\rceil$ times, then run $\calA$; size grows only quasi-polynomially while $k$ drops by a factor $f$.

nodes.name: Fix algorithm and diminisher
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a parameterized problem. Let $\calA$ be an algorithm that solves any instance~$(x,k)\in L$ in~$2^{c_1\cdot k}\cdot |x|^{c_2}$~time with constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and let~$\calD$ be a strong parameter diminisher for $L$ with constant~$d\geq 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Name the $2^{c_1k}|x|^{c_2}$ algorithm $\calA$ and the strong diminisher $\calD$ with factor $d\geq2$.

nodes.name: Introduce the growth constants and $f$
nodes.statement: Recall that by definition of a strong parameter diminisher, the size of the instance grows at most polynomially each time $\calD$ is applied. Let $b\geq 1$ be a constant such that the size of the instance obtained by applying $\calD$ once to $(x,k)$ is upper-bounded by $|x|^b$. We set~$\cmin:=\min\{2,b\}$. Let~$f:L\to\N$ be a function such that $f(x, k)\ge c$ for all $(x, k)\in L$ with $|x|\ge c_0$ for some constant~$c_0\in\N$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the size-growth exponent $b$, set $\cmin=\min\{2,b\}$, and fix the unbounded function $f$.

nodes.name: Bound the instance size
nodes.statement: Let $(x',k')$ be the instance of $L$ obtained by applying $\calD$ $\lceil\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)\rceil$ times to instance~$(x,k)\in L$ with $|x|\geq c_0$. We obtain \[ |x'| \leq |x|^{b^{\lceil\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)\rceil}} \leq |x|^{b^{2\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)}} \leq |x|^{f(x,k)^{c_3}},\, \text{for some constant $c_3\geq 1$.} \]
nodes.statement_short: Iterating $\calD$ that many times keeps $|x'|\leq|x|^{f(x,k)^{c_3}}$.

nodes.name: Bound the parameter
nodes.statement: Furthermore, the parameter decreases by the constant factor~$d$ each time the diminisher is applied, hence \[ k' = k/d^{\lceil\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)\rceil}\leq k/d^{\log_{\cmin} f(x,k)} \leq k/d^{\log_{d} f(x,k)}\leq k/f(x,k) . \]
nodes.statement_short: The same iteration drives the parameter to at most $k/f(x,k)$.

nodes.name: Run $\calA$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Finally, applying $\calA$ on $(x', k')$ solves $(x',k')$ in time \[2^{c_1\cdot k'}\cdot |x'|^{c_2} \leq 2^{c_1\cdot k/f(x,k)}\cdot |x|^{c_2\cdot f(x,k)^{c_3}} \in 2^{O(k/ f(x,k))}\cdot |x|^{f(x,k)^{O(1)}}.\qedhere\]
nodes.statement_short: Combining both bounds gives the claimed running time of $\calB$.

nodes.name: Proof for $k$-CNF-Sat($n$) under ETH
nodes.statement: \prob{$k$-CNF-Sat} can be solved in $O^*(2^{n})$ time via a brute-force algorithm~$\calA$, but does not admit a~$2^{o(n)}$ time algorithm under the~\ETH{}. By \Cref{lem:strdim} with algorithm~$\calA$ and~$f(\phi)=\log n$, \pprob{$k$-CNF-Sat}{n} does not admit a strong parameter diminisher unless the~\ETH{} breaks.
nodes.statement_short: Brute force meets the $2^{O(n)}$ hypothesis of the speed-up lemma; with $f=\log n$ a strong diminisher would beat ETH.

nodes.name: Matching upper and lower bounds
nodes.statement: \prob{$k$-CNF-Sat} can be solved in $O^*(2^{n})$ time via a brute-force algorithm~$\calA$, but does not admit a~$2^{o(n)}$ time algorithm under the~\ETH{}.
nodes.statement_short: Brute force gives $O^*(2^n)$; ETH forbids $2^{o(n)}$.

nodes.name: Apply the speed-up lemma
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lem:strdim} with algorithm~$\calA$ and~$f(\phi)=\log n$, \pprob{$k$-CNF-Sat}{n} does not admit a strong parameter diminisher unless the~\ETH{} breaks.
nodes.statement_short: With $f=\log n$ the lemma would yield a $2^{o(n)}$ algorithm.

nodes.name: Proof for Rooted Path($k$) under ETH
nodes.statement: \prob{Hamiltonian Path} on an $n$-vertex graph reduces trivially to \prob{Rooted Path} by adding a universal vertex and taking it as the root and setting the length of the path $k=n$. As \prob{Hamiltonian Path} does not admit a $2^{o(n)}$ time algorithm unless the~\ETH{} breaks~\cite{lokshtanov2011lower}, \prob{Rooted Path} does not admit a~$2^{o(n)}$ time algorithm unless the~\ETH{} breaks. There is an algorithm for \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} running in $2^{O(k)}\poly(n)$ time~\cite{AlonYZ95}. Let $(G=(V,E), k)$ be an instance of \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} and set~$f(G, k)=\log(|V|)=\log n$. By \Cref{lem:strdim} we get an algorithm for \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} running in~$2^{O(k/\log n)}\cdot |G|^{(\log n)^{O(1)}}\in 2^{o(n)}$ time. Hence, \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} does not admit a strong parameter diminisher unless the~\ETH{} breaks.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer the ETH lower bound from Hamiltonian Path, then apply the speed-up lemma with $f=\log n$.

nodes.name: Reduce Hamiltonian Path to Rooted Path
nodes.statement: \prob{Hamiltonian Path} on an $n$-vertex graph reduces trivially to \prob{Rooted Path} by adding a universal vertex and taking it as the root and setting the length of the path $k=n$.
nodes.statement_short: Add a universal vertex as root and set $k=n$.

nodes.name: Inherit the ETH lower bound
nodes.statement: As \prob{Hamiltonian Path} does not admit a $2^{o(n)}$ time algorithm unless the~\ETH{} breaks~\cite{lokshtanov2011lower}, \prob{Rooted Path} does not admit a~$2^{o(n)}$ time algorithm unless the~\ETH{} breaks.
nodes.statement_short: Rooted Path inherits the $2^{o(n)}$ lower bound.

nodes.name: Apply the speed-up lemma
nodes.statement: There is an algorithm for \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} running in $2^{O(k)}\poly(n)$ time~\cite{AlonYZ95}. Let $(G=(V,E), k)$ be an instance of \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} and set~$f(G, k)=\log(|V|)=\log n$. By \Cref{lem:strdim} we get an algorithm for \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} running in~$2^{O(k/\log n)}\cdot |G|^{(\log n)^{O(1)}}\in 2^{o(n)}$ time.
nodes.statement_short: With $f=\log n$ a strong diminisher would give a $2^{o(n)}$ algorithm.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, \pprob{Rooted Path}{k} does not admit a strong parameter diminisher unless the~\ETH{} breaks.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with ETH, so no strong diminisher exists.

nodes.name: Proof for Clique($\bw$) under ETH
nodes.statement: \prob{Clique} can be solved in $O^*(2^{\bw})$ time via a dynamic programming (brute-force) algorithm~$\calA$, but does not admit a $2^{o(n)}$ time algorithm under \ETH{}~\cite{lokshtanov2011lower}. Note that $\bw(G)\in O(n)$. By \Cref{lem:strdim} with algorithm $\calA$ and $f(G, k)=\log(|V|)=\log n$, \pprob{Clique}{\bw} does not admit a strong parameter diminisher unless the~\ETH{} breaks.
nodes.statement_short: Bandwidth dynamic programming matches the ETH bound, so the speed-up lemma with $f=\log n$ excludes a strong diminisher.
